Braun]]{{Cite web |url=https://www.habitas.org.uk/flora/species.asp?item=2007 |title=''Selaginella kraussiana'' |work=Flora of Northern Ireland |publisher=[[Ulster Museum]] |accessdate=2009-03-08}} | synonyms = ''Selaginella azorica'' G.Nicholson
''Selaginella canescens'' Fée | synonyms_ref = {{cite web|url= https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:90781-3|title= Selaginella kraussiana (Kunze) A.Braun|author=|date=n.d.|website=Plants of the World Online|publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew|access-date= September 25, 2020}} }} '''''Selaginella kraussiana''''' is a species of [[vascular plant]] in the family [[Selaginellaceae]]. It is referred to by the common names '''Krauss' spikemoss''',{{PLANTS|id=SEKR|taxon=Selaginella kraussiana|accessdate=9 November 2015}} '''Krauss's clubmoss''',{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }} or '''African clubmoss''', and is found naturally in parts of [[Sub-Saharan Africa]] and in [[Macaronesia]].{{cite web | title=GBIF ''Selaginella kraussiana'' (Kunze) A. Braun|url=https://www.gbif.org/species/2688189 | publisher=Global Biodiversity Information System | location=Copenhagen, Denmark }} It is sometimes given the misnomer of "peacock fern", due to its lacy leaf structure, despite having no relation to actual [[ferns]]; rather, it belongs to the very ancient lineage of plants known as the [[Lycopodiophyta|clubmosses]]. ==Description== Growing to just {{convert|5|cm|in|abbr=on}} high, it is a low-growing, mat-forming [[evergreen]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] with primitive fern-like leaves, that spreads via rooting stems. Seginella kraussiana.jpg|Illustrating greener coloration when grown in brighter light Selaginella kraussiana OB10.1.jpg|Close-up of the foliage ==Distribution== Its native distribution is the [[Macaronesia]], and parts of south and east [[Africa]]. Its native distribution in the [[Azores]] was controversial up until 2005, when spores of this species were discovered in 6,000-year-old fossils on [[Pico Island|Pico]].{{cite web |title=Selaginella kraussiana (Kunze) A.Braun |url=https://acores.flora-on.pt/#/1selaginella+kraussiana |publisher=[[Flora-On]] |access-date=25 August 2021}}{{cite web |last1=Araújo |first1=Paulo V. |last2=Carvalho |first2=Maria P. |title=Nas asas do vento |url=https://dias-com-arvores.blogspot.com/2010/12/nas-asas-do-vento.html |access-date=25 August 2021 |date=2010}} Since its introduction to Britain in 1878 it has spread slowly, and was first recorded in the wild in 1917 in west [[Cornwall]] (UK) and [[County Leitrim]] (Ireland), often as a greenhouse weed.{{cite web|url=https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/index.php?q=node/2409|title=Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora, ''Selaginella kraussiana'' (Kraus's Clubmoss)|publisher=Biological Records Centre and Botanical Society of Britain and Ireland }} ''Selaginella kraussiana'' is listed on the [[New Zealand]] [[National Pest Plant Accord]] since it is an [[invasive species]]. It is common in many parts of New Zealand and Australia where it forms dense mats in shaded areas.[http://floraseries.landcareresearch.co.nz/pages/Taxon.aspx?id=_56635f7d-52d7-49c7-8d2e-b6cd17bb1e4a&fileName=Flora%204.xml ''Flora of New Zealand'']{{Cite book|last1=Brownsey|first1=Patrick John|url=https://datastore.landcareresearch.co.nz/dataset/1af4a5bc-4afc-4beb-bc5a-b033466a41ac/resource/67299c97-d336-45ac-bd72-c5edc4ff89fa/download/floraofnewzealand-ferns-21-brownseyperrie-2018-selaginellaceae.pdf|title=Selaginellaceae|last2=Perrie|first2=Leon Richard|publisher=Manaaki Whenua-Landcare Research New Zealand Ltd.|year=2018|isbn=978-0-947525-41-5|location=Lincoln, New Zealand|pages=3–5|doi=10.7931/B18S6Q|oclc=1082892769}} ==Cultivation== ''Selaginella kraussiana'' is cultivated for ornamental purposes.{{GRIN | accessdate = 19 January 2018}} It requires a minimum temperature of {{convert|5|C|F|abbr=on}}, and in [[temperateness|temperate]] regions is grown under glass as a [[houseplant]]. The species{{cite web|title=''Selaginella kraussiana'' | url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/17035/Selaginella-kraussiana/Details | publisher=Royal Horticultural Society|accessdate=8 March 2021}} and the [[cultivar]] 'Brownii'{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/74498/i-Selaginella-kraussiana-i-Brownii/Details | title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Selaginella kraussiana'' 'Brownii' | accessdate = 7 November 2018}} have both gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 96 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 8 November 2018}} Other cultivars include 'Aurea' and 'Gold Tips'. They prefer a sheltered spot, in full or partial shade. They require potting media that retains humidity while not staying overly wet, and drains quickly. An acidic to neutral pH (6.0–7.0) is preferable. In the winter, a cultivar often referred to as ''Selaginella kraussiana'' 'Frosty Fern' is sold as a [[house plant]] due to its white-tipped foliage; however, this is more often the taller-growing ''[[Selaginella martensii]]'', not the shorter, creeping ''S. kraussiana''.{{citation needed|date=January 2023}} ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== * {{Commons category-inline|Selaginella kraussiana|''Selaginella kraussiana''}} * {{Wikispecies-inline|Selaginella kraussiana|''Selaginella kraussiana''}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q7447419}} [[Category:Selaginella|kraussiana]] [[Category:Flora of Africa]] [[Category:Flora of the Azores]] [[Category:Flora of the Canary Islands]] [[Category:Taxa named by Alexander Braun]] [[Category:Taxa named by Gustav Kunze]] {{Lycophyte-stub}}
